name: Sertraline Hydrochloride
sections: White crystalline powder (hydrochloride), slightly soluble in water.
Developed by Pfizer scientists from the early 1970s, evolving from neuroleptic chemical structures. First approval/introduction: US FDA 1991 (Pfizer).

Potent and selective inhibitor of neuronal serotonin reuptake with weak dopamine reuptake inhibition; minimal affinity for adrenergic, cholinergic or histaminergic receptors. Receptor / target profile: Selective SERT inhibitor (Ki 0.15–3.3 nM) with weaker dopamine transporter inhibition and sigma-1 binding.
Hepatic N-demethylation (mainly CYP2B6; also CYP2C19 and others) to desmethylsertraline
Summary: Slowly absorbed; Tmax 4.5–8.4 h. ~98% protein bound. Extensive first-pass metabolism (multiple CYPs) to weakly active desmethylsertraline. Half-life ~26 h.
Major depressive disorder and prevention of relapse
Depression / OCD: 50 mg once daily; increase in 50 mg steps at ≥1-week intervals; max 200 mg/day
Panic / PTSD / social anxiety: start 25 mg once daily for 1 week, then 50 mg/day
Once daily, morning or evening, with or without food
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Use lower or less frequent doses.
Standard dose with caution; monitor sodium.
One of the more widely used SSRIs in pregnancy; use only if clearly needed.
Low milk transfer; generally considered compatible with breastfeeding under supervision.
Taper on discontinuation; caution in hepatic impairment
With or without food; oral concentrate contains latex/alcohol in some brands; avoid alcohol.
Mood/suicidality; sodium; bleeding risk with anticoagulants.
Somnolence, GI upset, tachycardia, tremor, agitation, serotonin syndrome. Supportive care.
SADHART (JAMA 2002) – sertraline safe and effective for depression after acute coronary syndrome.
CAMS (NEJM 2008) – sertraline plus CBT most effective in paediatric anxiety.
Cipriani et al., Lancet 2009 (MANGA) – favourable efficacy–acceptability balance.
Take once daily at the same time
GI upset early is common – take after food
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
